page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, but does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers modest compute capabilities, with both single-core and multi-core CPU performance falling into the lower 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show 205.76 GB/sec for cached reads and approximately 26.28 GB/sec for uncached reads. While database operations and Redis SET performance of 3.61 million operations per second are relatively low, the instance achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and Passmark memory tests.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency compute power. It is well-suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, memory-bound enterprise applications, and lightweight data processing tasks where RAM capacity is the primary constraint.

Benchmark results place its compute performance, including Geekbench and stress-ng scores, in the lower quartile, though it maintains average performance in memory benchmarks and single-threaded gzip compression. It is best suited for small databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
